title: PdfTextExtract
description: Sidecar record for one PDF turned into plain text on disk. Says what was extracted, by what, from which bytes, and what could not be done. Written next to the text files it describes; a reader consults it to decide whether the text is worth loading and how far it can be trusted. Not an index and not evidence — it records an extraction, nothing about the biology in it.

extract_version.description: Bumped when the sidecar shape changes in a way that invalidates existing extractions.

retrieval_method.description: How this text was obtained. Fixed to `pdf_text` so downstream consumers can tell PDF-derived text from JATS. It matters: pymupdf4llm does not reliably preserve reading order across columns, so a quote spliced across a column boundary can still pass a substring check against this text. Do not treat it as equivalent to JATS for quote grounding.

segments.description: Body paragraphs in the order they appear in the body text file, each tagged with the nearest preceding heading and located by character offset so a caller can read one section without loading the file.

figure_segments.description: Figure-internal text (axis labels, panel tags, gene-name strips), located in the figure text file. Kept apart from the body so it can be indexed for recall without ever being quoted as prose — it has no sentence structure and no reliable order.

gaps.description: What the extractor could not do, stated explicitly so an absence is never read as a negative result. An image-only PDF produces an empty text file and a gap here, not a silent success.

Source.description: The PDF the text came from, identified by content rather than by name so a re-extraction can tell whether the file changed.

filename.description: Base name of the source PDF.

path.description: Path the extractor was pointed at, as given. May be relative; the sha256 is the reliable identifier.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the source PDF bytes.

n_pages.description: Page count reported by the PDF itself, independent of how much text came out. A large n_pages with n_chars near zero is the signature of a scanned document.

Extractor.description: What produced the text, pinned so an extraction can be reproduced or invalidated when the library changes.

version.description: Installed version, or null when the library does not report one.

extracted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the extraction.

Outputs.description: The files written and how much text is in them. Paths are relative to the directory holding this sidecar.

text_file.description: Body text: paragraphs separated by blank lines, no markup. Offsets in `segments` index into this file.

figure_text_file.description: Figure-internal text, or null when the PDF had none or figure text was not requested.

Segment.description: One paragraph, located in its text file. `text_file[char_start:char_end]` is exactly the paragraph.

section.description: Nearest preceding heading in the PDF, `BODY` before the first heading, `IN_FIGURE` for figure-internal text. Headings come from the PDF's own typography and are not normalised to any vocabulary.

Gap.description: Something the extraction could not deliver.

kind.description: `no_text_extracted`: the PDF yielded no body prose at all, most often a scanned or image-only document (there is no OCR here). `figure_text_only`: the only text found was inside figures. `short_text`: some prose came out but far less than the page count suggests, so parts of the document are likely unreadable. `extractor_error`: the library failed on part of the file.

detail.description: What happened, in enough detail for a human to decide what to do next.
